# Lab 10.4: BigQuery-Managed Apache Iceberg Tables

## What We Are Going to Do
Create an Apache Iceberg table that BigQuery manages, write to it with DML, and export its Iceberg metadata so other engines can read it.

## Steps

1. **[CLI] Let the connection write to the bucket.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SA=$(bq show --format=json --connection $PROJECT_ID.us.lab_conn | python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['cloudResource']['serviceAccountId'])")
gcloud storage buckets add-iam-policy-binding gs://$PROJECT_ID-bq-labs \
  --member=serviceAccount:$SA --role=roles/storage.objectAdmin</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[SQL] Create the Iceberg table.** Replace `YOUR_PROJECT` and `YOUR_BUCKET`.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE TABLE lab10.orders_iceberg (
  order_id INT64,
  user_id INT64,
  status STRING,
  created_at TIMESTAMP
)
CLUSTER BY status
WITH CONNECTION `YOUR_PROJECT.us.lab_conn`
OPTIONS (
  file_format = 'PARQUET',
  table_format = 'ICEBERG',
  storage_uri = 'gs://YOUR_BUCKET/iceberg/orders'
);</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[SQL] Write with DML.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">INSERT INTO lab10.orders_iceberg
SELECT order_id, user_id, status, created_at
FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.orders`
WHERE created_at &gt;= '2025-01-01';

UPDATE lab10.orders_iceberg SET status = 'Archived' WHERE created_at &lt; '2025-02-01';
SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM lab10.orders_iceberg GROUP BY status;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **[SQL] Export Iceberg metadata.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">EXPORT TABLE METADATA FROM lab10.orders_iceberg;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


5. **[CLI] Look at the open files.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH

<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud storage ls -r gs://$PROJECT_ID-bq-labs/iceberg/orders/ | head -20</span>
</code></pre>

   You see `data/` Parquet files and `metadata/` JSON files. Spark, Trino or Flink can read the table from the metadata file.

6. **[Console] Check the details.** Open `orders_iceberg → Details`. It shows **Table format: ICEBERG** and the storage URI.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Storage | Parquet files in your bucket |
| Writes | Full DML from BigQuery |
| Maintenance | Compaction and cleanup done by BigQuery |
| Interoperability | Exported Iceberg metadata for other engines |
